newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PCI Bank closes US$75 mln FRCD.
newsitem.headline: PCI Bank closes US$75 mln FRCD.

text.p: Philippine Commercial International Bank's US$75 million floating rate certificates of deposit issue due 1999 has been closed, arranger Chase Manhattan Asia said Friday.
The three-year certificates were issued at par and re-offered at 99.80. They pay a coupon of 75 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the all-in return for top-tier manager is 85 basis points.
The certificates were issued under the borrower's US$500 million Global Medium Term Note Programme.
Arranger and lead manager Chase Manhattan Asia committed to US$28 million.
Co-arrangers, with US$7 million each, are Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and JP Morgan Securities Asia.
Senior managers, with US$4 million each, are Bank Austria's Singapore branch and Berliner Bank.

Managers are ASEAN Finance Corp, PT Bank Negara Indonesia's Singapore branch, Thai Farmers Bank's Singapore branch and United Malayan Banking Corp's Singapore branch, with US$3 million each, and Bank Brussels Lambert, Grand Commercial Bank and Landesbank Rheinland-Pfalz Girozentrale, with US$2 million each.
Signing is set for November 20 in Hong Kong. The payment date is November 27.
